currentUse: The former Ss. Peter and Paul church at 307 Pine Street remains an active Roman Catholic worship site as St. John XXIII Parish. St. John XXIII was formed by unifying Ss. Peter and Paul with St. Jerome after the Lithuanian parish's pastor retired in 2014. Both churches initially remained open; St. Jerome later closed, and the successor parish consolidated in the Ss. Peter and Paul building. This is an institutional merger with host-site continuity, not an uninterrupted Ss. Peter and Paul parish under a new name. The former parish's cemetery remains in successor-parish care on Owl Creek Road.
summary: Ss. Peter and Paul was Tamaqua's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish. The official successor history describes a small Lithuanian church founded on Pine Street in 1913; an earlier 1911 organizing date survives in the canonical registry and remains a formation-phase variant. A combined church-school building was begun in 1927. The present worship complex is at 307 Pine Street, where a later church interior incorporated work by Lithuanian-American artist and architect Vytautas Kazimieras Jonynas. After longtime pastor Father William Linkchorst retired in 2014, Ss. Peter and Paul and St. Jerome were unified as St. John XXIII Parish. Both buildings initially remained open, but St. Jerome later closed and the successor parish consolidated in the former Ss. Peter and Paul building, which was remodeled with furnishings from both predecessor churches. The institution ended through merger while its building, cemetery, and worship-site function continued in distinct forms.

historicalNarrative.text: Tamaqua's Lithuanian Catholic institution took visible form on Pine Street in the early 1910s. The official St. John XXIII parish history calls Ss. Peter and Paul a small Lithuanian Catholic church founded in 1913. The inherited registry also carries 1911 as a parish-organizing date. Until a contemporary erection or dedication record is located, the safe reading is an organizing phase by 1911 followed by the Pine Street church foundation in 1913, rather than two different institutions.

historicalNarrative.text: A new combined church-school building was begun in 1927 and opened later. It stands behind the later church at 307 Pine Street and survives as part of the parish complex. The main church later received a distinctive Lithuanian modern interior by artist-architect Vytautas Kazimieras Jonynas; field documentation dates that work to 1976. These are successive buildings within the same parish complex and should not be mistaken for separate Ss. Peter and Paul institutions.

historicalNarrative.text: Father William Linkchorst served Ss. Peter and Paul for thirty years and retired in 2014. At that point Ss. Peter and Paul and St. Jerome remained open as worship sites but were unified into the new St. John XXIII Parish under Father John Frink. Later operating costs and the repair needs of St. Jerome's building led to its closure. St. John XXIII then consolidated in the former Ss. Peter and Paul church, which was remodeled using relics, furniture, and woodwork from both predecessor churches.

historicalNarrative.text: As of August 2026 St. John XXIII advertises regular Saturday, Sunday, and weekday Masses at 307 Pine Street, confirming active hosted worship in the former Lithuanian church. The successor parish also maintains Ss. Peter and Paul Cemetery on Owl Creek Road, about one-quarter mile south of Tamaqua off Route 309. Active worship and cemetery care are continuities of site and stewardship; the former Ss. Peter and Paul institution itself does not remain separately active after the merger.

developments.headline: Lithuanian Catholics establish Ss. Peter and Paul on Pine Street
developments.detail: The registry preserves an organizing date of 1911, while the official successor history dates the small Pine Street Lithuanian church to 1913.

developments.headline: Combined church-school building begins
developments.detail: The parish began a new combined church and school structure on Pine Street; that earlier building survives behind the current church.

developments.headline: Ss. Peter and Paul merges into St. John XXIII
developments.detail: After Father Linkchorst retired, Ss. Peter and Paul and St. Jerome became one parish. St. Jerome later closed, and the successor consolidated in the former Ss. Peter and Paul building.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The official successor history says the small Pine Street church was founded in 1913, while the registry previously selected 1911 from an earlier official-history reading. These are retained as an organizing-versus-church-foundation ambiguity until a contemporary source is located. St. John XXIII is a distinct merger successor; the continued use of the former Ss. Peter and Paul building and cemetery does not mean the Lithuanian parish remained institutionally unchanged.
gaps: The canonical erection and first dedication records, exact opening date of the 1927 building, date and documentation for the later main church, full Jonynas commission and 1976 dedication records, exact merger decree and effective date, St. Jerome closure date, sacramental-record custody, and the full cemetery establishment chronology remain to be located.
